a: The selected applicant is required to submit the bank guarantee of the prescribed amount along with an undertaking within two weeks from the date of issuance of the approval letter.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware
q: What is the objective of the scheme?
a: The scheme aims to boost domestic manufacturing and attract large investments in the IT hardware value chain.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware
q: Which ministry has launched this scheme?
a: The scheme has been launched by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware
q: What products are covered under the scheme?
a: The scheme covers laptops, tablets, all-in-one PCs, and servers.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware
q: What type of benefit is provided under the scheme?
a: The scheme provides a production-linked incentive on net incremental sales of eligible goods manufactured in India.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware
q: What is the incentive rate under the scheme?
a: An incentive of 4% to 2% / 1% is provided on net incremental sales over the base year.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware
q: What is the duration of the scheme?
a: The incentive is provided for a period of 4 years.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware
q: Who can apply under the scheme?
a: Companies registered in India and engaged in manufacturing eligible IT hardware products can apply, subject to meeting scheme criteria.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware
q: How is the scheme implemented?
a: The scheme is implemented through a Nodal Agency acting as a Project Management Agency (PMA).

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware
q: On what basis is the incentive provided?
a: The incentive is provided based on net incremental sales of eligible products over the base year.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware Scheme 2.O
q: What products are covered under the "Target Segment" of this scheme?
a: The target segment includes Laptops, Tablets, All-in-One Personal Computers (PCs), Servers, and Ultra Small Form Factor (USSF) devices. To be eligible, these must be manufactured in India and be complete in all respects for sale to consumers.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware Scheme 2.O
q: Who is considered an "Applicant" under the scheme?
a: An applicant is a company registered in India that proposes to manufacture goods covered under the target segment and submits an application for approval. Manufacturing can occur at new or existing facilities across one or more locations in India.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware Scheme 2.O
q: What are the different categories of companies that can apply?
a: There are three categories: | - Global Company: Non-domestic companies with high global manufacturing revenue.- Domestic Company: Companies owned by resident Indian citizens (more than 50% capital).- Hybrid (Global/Domestic) Company: A category where both global and domestic companies can apply based on specific revenue thresholds

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware Scheme 2.O
q: What types of investments are eligible for determining threshold criteria?
a: Eligible investments include expenditure on Plant, Machinery, Equipment, and Associated Utilities (including tools, dies, moulds, etc.), Research and Development (R&D), and Transfer of Technology (ToT) agreements. Expenditure on land and buildings is explicitly excluded.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware Scheme 2.O
q: Are there mandatory localization requirements?
a: Yes. Applicants are required to localise at least Printed Circuit Board Assembly (PCBA) and the assembly of the finished goods starting from the first year. In each subsequent year, at least one additional component or sub-assembly must be localised.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware Scheme 2.O
q: How is the incentive calculated if there is an investment shortfall?
a: If the cumulative investment shortfall is 40% or less of the required threshold, the applicant remains eligible. However, the incentive for that year will be reduced by half of the percentage of the shortfall (e.g., a 30% shortfall results in a 15% incentive deduction).

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware Scheme 2.O
q: Can an applicant claim incentives for products manufactured through a contract manufacturer?
a: Yes, incentives can be claimed on sales of goods manufactured through a contract manufacturer, provided the arrangement is exclusive for the PLI applicant and the contract manufacturer has not claimed incentives for the same goods under any other PLI scheme.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware Scheme 2.O
q: What happens if an applicant’s actual incentive claim is much lower than their projection?
a: To ensure realistic targets, penalties apply: a 5% deduction if the shortfall is between 25% and 50% of the projection, and a 10% deduction if the shortfall exceeds 50% of the projection. No penalty applies if no incentive is payable for that year.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware Scheme 2.O
q: Is there a limit on the total incentive an applicant can receive?
a: Yes, there is an overall ceiling on the total incentive payable to any applicant during the scheme's tenure. This ceiling includes incentives gained from over-performance and any incentives received under the previous PLI Scheme 1.0 for IT Hardware.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry
q: Who is an applicant under the scheme?
a: An applicant under the scheme is a | i. Company incorporated/ registered in India under the Companies Act, 2013, engaged in the automotive and/or auto component manufacturing sector or | ii. New Non-Automotive Investor company (who is currently not in an automobile or auto component manufacturing business) incorporated/ registered in India under the Companies Act, 2013 meeting the eligibility criteria specified under the scheme and making an application for seeking approval under the Scheme.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry
q: What are the circumstances under which an applicant may be ineligible for the scheme?
a: The applicants whose accounts are declared as Non-Performing Asset | (NPA) as per RBI guidelines or defaulter or wilful defaulter as per RBI/CIBIL | or SEBI debarred list or reported as fraud by any bank, financial institution | or non-banking financial companies etc. would be considered ineligible. | Further, there should not be any insolvency proceedings admitted against | the Applicant in the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) etc.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry
q: Can an applicant have multiple manufacturing facilities?
a: An applicant can have multiple manufacturing facilities/ locations in India.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry
q: Are Greenfield projects and Brownfield projects both allowed under the scheme?
a: Yes, Greenfield projects and Brownfield projects both are allowed under the | scheme.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry

a: No, Proprietorship, Partnership, and LLPs are not allowed under the scheme. Any company incorporated in India and as defined in the Companies Act 2 of 16 2013, proposing to manufacture one or more eligible product(s) under the scheme, can be an applicant.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry
q: Can a 100% foreign-owned company be eligible under PLI Scheme?
a: Yes, but it has to be registered in India to apply under the scheme.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry
q: Do the Value-Added Resellers and Trading companies which are not in manufacturing business qualify under the scheme?
a: Yes, any Company registered in India under the Companies Act can apply under the scheme subject to meeting the eligibility criteria and establishing a manufacturing facility for production of the eligible products under the scheme.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry
q: Can two or more companies of the Group apply through a single common Application?
a: Any number of companies of the Group is permitted to apply under this scheme as an individual applicants by submitting separate applications. However, they can use the global group revenue, gross block, and net worth of the Group in their separate applications respectively.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry
q: How many components are there in this scheme?
a: There are two components in the scheme i. Champion OEM incentive scheme ii. Component Champion incentive scheme

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry
q: Can a company submit Multiple Applications as Applicant under different Categories?
a: An applicant eligible for applying under Champion OEM can also apply for the Component Champion segment. However, an auto component manufacturer as an applicant eligible for applying under the Component Champion segment cannot apply under Champion OEM.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry
q: Can an applicant approved under both Champion OEM and Component Champion segment claim incentive for the same component under both segments?
a: An approved legal entity as an Automotive OEM company or New NonAutomotive Investor company can avail incentives under both components of the scheme subject to the condition that any eligible product shall be incentivized only once under the scheme. Any double claim of incentive for the same product under component level and vehicle level can lead to the qualification of the legal entity involved on this ground alone in addition to any other legal action as applicable under the law.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry

a: This is a fund-limited scheme. In case the calculated incentive pay-out exceeds the budgetary outlay, the scheme could be exhausted earlier than 5 (Five) years period and the incentive pay-out will be reduced on a pro-rata basis as per the formulation developed across all PLIs.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry
q: Is there any segregation in the budgetary outlay based on vehicle segments like 2W, 3W, 4W, CV, Tractors and Vehicles used for military purpose etc.?
a: No. There is only one allocation in the scheme.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry
q: Is there any segregation in the budgetary outlay for vehicles and Auto components in the scheme?
a: No. There is only one allocation in the scheme.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry
q: What is the period for making an application under the Scheme?
a: The window for receiving applications through the online portal of the scheme shall be 60 days starting from the date of Notice Inviting Applications.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry
q: What is the base year for calculation of eligible sale value?
a: Financial Year 2019-20 shall be treated as the base year for calculating eligible sale value (not applicable for approved new non-automotive investor companies).

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry
q: Can any applicant company claim incentive for any Automobile or Auto component manufactured by them?
a: No. The applicant company once selected and approved under the scheme can claim an incentive on the Determined sales value of eligible Advanced Automotive Technology products prescribed by MHI.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry
q: Can any approved company claim scheme incentive for all Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) products manufactured by them?
a: Any approved company can claim incentive under the scheme for only those Advanced Automotive Technology products meeting the condition of minimum 50% domestic value addition.

n: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Automobile And Auto Component Industry
q: When can an applicant submit a claim for disbursements under PLI?
a: An applicant may submit a claim for disbursement of incentive within 6 (six) months from the end of the financial year to which the claim pertains or within 3 (three) months from the date of finalization of Audited Financial Statements for the same financial year, whichever is later. Claim for any financial year period shall be made only once, unless withdrawn, and no subsequent part claims shall be allowed for the said period.

n: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for White Goods (Air Conditioners and LED Lights)
q: What financial benefit does the PLI Scheme for White Goods provide
a: It offers 4%–6% incentive on net incremental sales of eligible products over the base year for 5 years.

n: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for White Goods (Air Conditioners and LED Lights)
q: How does the scheme support domestic manufacturing?
a: It encourages investment in new manufacturing facilities for AC and LED components, boosting localization and reducing imports.

n: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for White Goods (Air Conditioners and LED Lights)

a: Yes. Up to 40% of incremental sales of eligible products may be to sectors outside AC/LED, enabling economies of scale.

n: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for White Goods (Air Conditioners and LED Lights)

a: Yes. Companies can invest in multiple eligible components within a target segment; backward integration investments are also eligible.

n: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for White Goods (Air Conditioners and LED Lights)

a: Yes. Captive consumption counts as net sales turnover if at least 60% goes into AC/LED manufacturing.

n: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for White Goods (Air Conditioners and LED Lights)

a: Incentives are disbursed the year after meeting both investment and sales thresholds, provided that the requisite conditions are met

n: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for White Goods (Air Conditioners and LED Lights)
q: Who can apply under the PLI White Goods Scheme?
a: Only companies incorporated in India under the Companies Act (2013 or 1956). LLPs cannot apply.

n: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for White Goods (Air Conditioners and LED Lights)

n: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for White Goods (Air Conditioners and LED Lights)

a: No. Double benefits for the same product across PLI schemes are not allowed

n: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for White Goods (Air Conditioners and LED Lights)

a: Applications must be submitted online via the PLI-WG portal.

n: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for White Goods (Air Conditioners and LED Lights)
q: What is the application window?
a: The scheme opens applications for specified windows; initial was 15 June–15 Sept 2021 with possible later rounds.

n: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for White Goods (Air Conditioners and LED Lights)
q: What is the application fee and payment mode?
a: Rs 1,00,000 to be paid online

n: Pradhan Mantri Dakshta Aur Kushalta Sampann Hitgrahi (PM-DAKSH)
q: What is the main objective of PM-DAKSH Yojana?
a: The main objective of the PM-DAKSH Yojana is to increase the skill levels of the target youth by providing them short term and long term skills, followed by assistance in wage/self-employment. Besides above, the skill levels of artisans would be enhanced through Upskilling/Reskilling programmes and enable them to increase their incomes within their practicing vocations.

n: Pradhan Mantri Dakshta Aur Kushalta Sampann Hitgrahi (PM-DAKSH)
q: Who is eligible for the PM-DAKSH Yojana?

n: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthan Mahabhiyan Scheme For Farmers.
q: What Are The Different Kind Of Systems Supported Under PM-KUSUM Scheme?
a: PM-KUSUM Scheme supports three different kind of installations, known as three components of the Scheme as given below: | Component-A: Setting up of decentralized ground/ stilt mounted grid connected solar or other renewable energy based power plants up to 2 MW capacity | Component-B: Installation of stand-alone solar agriculture pumps of capacity up to 7.5 HP | Component-C: Solarisation of existing grid connected agriculture pumps of capacity up to 7.5 HP

n: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthan Mahabhiyan Scheme For Farmers.
q: What Is Component-A Of PM-KUSUM Scheme?
a: Under this component, solar or other renewable energy based power plants of capacity 500 kW to 2 MW can be installed on barren or uncultivable agriculture land mainly. Agriculture land is also permitted under this scheme provided that solar plants are installed in slit fashion (i.e. raised structure for installation of solar panels) and with adequate spacing between panel rows for ensuring that farming activity is not affected.

n: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthan Mahabhiyan Scheme For Farmers.
q: Who Is Eligible Under Component-A Of PM-KUSUM Scheme?
a: Individual farmers/ group of farmers/ cooperatives/panchayats/ Farmer Producer Organisations (FPO)/Water User associations (WUA). Land on which the project is proposed to be installed should be within 5 km from the nearest electricity sub-station.

n: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthan Mahabhiyan Scheme For Farmers.
q: Who Will Purchase The Generated Electricity?
a: Power generated will be purchased by the local electricity distribution companies (Discoms)

n: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthan Mahabhiyan Scheme For Farmers.
q: Can Farmers Lease Their Land For The Development Of Renewable Energy Power Plant Under Component-A?
a: Yes, farmers can either install renewable power project on their land or lease the land on rent to a developer at mutually agreed terms between the parties.

n: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthan Mahabhiyan Scheme For Farmers.
q: What Kind Of Financial Support Is Available Under Component-A Of The Scheme?
a: The renewable power generated will be purchased by DISCOMs at a pre-fixed levelised tariff. The duration of PPA will be 25 years from Commercial Operation Date (COD) of the project. Procurement based incentive (PBI) of 40 paisa per unit of electricity generated or Rs. 6.6 lakh per MW per annum, whichever is lower, will be provided to DISCOM for buying electricity generated for five years.

n: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthan Mahabhiyan Scheme For Farmers.

a: Under this Component, farmers can replace their existing diesel poweredagriculture pumps with standalone solar pumpsof capacity up to 7.5 HP in off-grid areas. Pumps of capacity higher than 7.5 HP may be allowed, however, the central subsidy will be limited to the subsidy applicable for pump of 7.5 HP.

n: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthan Mahabhiyan Scheme For Farmers.

a: Individual farmers, Water User Associations and community/cluster based irrigation system will be covered under this component.

For North-eastern States, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir/Ladakh and Island UTs, subsidy of 50% will be provided by Central Government and at least 30% will be provided by the State Government for installation of solar pump. n: PM Street Vendor’s AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi)

n: PM Street Vendor’s AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi)

n: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan
q: What is PM-SYM?
a: PM-SYM is a voluntary and contributory pension scheme for unorganized workers.

n: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan
q: Who can apply the scheme?
a: Unorganized workers aged 18 to 40 years with a monthly income of up to ₹15,000 can join the scheme.

n: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan
q: What pension amount is provided?
a: A minimum assured pension of ₹3,000 per month is provided after attaining 60 years of age.

n: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan
q: Is government contribution provided?
a: Yes, the Central Government provides an equal matching contribution to the subscriber.

n: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan
q: Is Aadhaar mandatory?
a: Yes, Aadhaar is mandatory for enrollment under PM-SYM.

n: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan
q: Can a Jan-Dhan account be used?
a: Yes, a Jan-Dhan account can be used for enrollment and contribution.

n: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan
q: Is the scheme voluntary?
a: Yes, enrollment under PM-SYM is completely voluntary.

n: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan
q: What happens if the subscriber dies after 60 years?
a: The spouse is entitled to receive a family pension equal to 50% of the pension amount.

n: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan
q: What happens if the subscriber dies before 60 years?
a: The spouse may continue the scheme by paying contributions or withdraw the accumulated amount with interest.

n: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan
q: Can contributions be regularized if missed?
a: Yes, missed contributions can be regularized by paying outstanding dues with applicable penalties.

n: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan
q: Is online enrollment available?
a: Yes, online enrollment is available through the PM-SYM portal or mobile application.

n: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan
q: Who manages the pension fund?
a: The pension fund is managed by the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC).

n: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan
q: Where can enrollment be done?
a: Enrollment can be done at the nearest Common Services Centre (CSC).

n: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan
q: Is the scheme applicable to EPFO or ESIC members?
a: No, workers covered under EPFO or ESIC are not eligible for the scheme.

n: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan

a: The nearest CSC can be located by visiting locator.csccloud.in.

n: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana - Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh

n: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana - Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh

For Medical students NEET counseling for availing benefits under the scheme SSSJKL. For B.Sc.(Nursing) students, NEET is also mandatory wherever applicable.

n: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana - Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh

n: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana - Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh

n: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana - Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh

n: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana - Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh
q: I Have Filled & Submitted My Online Application Form. What Should I Do Next?
a: Take printout of online filled application and visit your nearest facilitation centre along with original documents & one set of self-attested photocopies of all original documents for verification. The details are given in AICTE website.

n: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana - Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh

a: You can go to any one of the nearest facilitation centers established by Govt. of UTs of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh as per your convenience for document verification and after that choice filling option would be open. (List of Facilitation Centers is available at AICTE Website).

n: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana - Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh

n: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana - Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh

n: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana - Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh

a: Yes, you may call on 011-29581043/07/51/10 (from 9.30 am to 5.00 pm Monday to Friday) or email at pmsss_cell@aicte-india.org on all working days for any queries. You can also register your grievance from your login to get the resolution for your query.

n: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana - Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh

n: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana - Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh

n: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana - Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh

n: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana: Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme
q: What is the objective of "Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme (CSIS)”?
a: CSIS is a unique scheme which pivots around the vision that no student desiring to pursue higher education is denied of the opportunity if he/ she is financially poor. This scheme benefits all categories of economically weaker students for pursuing professional/ technical courses in India only and intends to provide affordable higher education. The Scheme envisages uplifting the students from the grassroots level and increasing the number of qualified technicians/ professionals in the nation. CSIS aims to check the existing geographical imbalance with regard to the Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER)

n: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana: Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme
q: Who is eligible for the scheme?
a: • Students who want to pursue Technical/Professional higher education courses in recognized institutes in India. | • Higher Education Institutions (HEI) should be NAAC, NBA, CFTI accredited or regulatory approved institutes in India.

n: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana: Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme

n: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
q: What are the components supported under the scheme?
a: i. Skilling and Training (Non-traditional and traditional) | ii. Women Leadership and Entrepreneurship | iii. Education (through National Institute of Open Schooling) | iv. Infrastructure Development (through Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram)

n: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
q: What are the skills taught under the scheme?
a: Any of the skills approved by the NSQC and registered under the National Qualification Register (NQR) are eligible to be provided under the scheme.

n: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
q: Is there any stipend provided under the scheme?
a: Yes. | Rs.3000/- per month for beneficiaries undertaking traditional skilling, | Rs. 2000/- per month for beneficiaries undertaking non-traditional (modern) skilling in non residential mode, | Rs. 1000/- per month for beneficiaries undertaking non-traditional (modern) skilling in residential mode (Max 12 months) | Rs. 1000/- for beneficiaries enrolled under education component (Max 6 months), | Rs. 200/- per day for beneficiaries under women leadership and entrepreneurship component

n: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
q: Does the scheme involves linking trained and certified candidates in modern skilling with placement opportunities?
a: Placement of minimum 75% of beneficiaries trained under modern skilling are to be ensured by the implementing agency post completion of training program, with at least 50% of them in organised as categorized in the National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF)/ Common Cost Norms (CCN) of Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.

n: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
q: Who are eligible for benefiting under the scheme?
a: Six notified communities under the NCM Act, i.e., Buddhists, Christian, Jains, Muslims, Parsis and Sikhs are eligible for applying under the scheme. However, up to 25% of seats may be earmarked under traditional skilling and up to 15% under other components for non minority EWS category.

n: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
q: What is the educational qualification required under the scheme?
a: The educational qualification for Skilling and Training component would be as per National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF) norms and Education component would be as per National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) norms. Candidates with aptitude and leadership qualities will be selected for Women Leadership and Entrepreneurship component.

n: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
q: Are there any seats earmarked for women candidates?
a: 33% in Skilling and Training component, 50% in Education component and 100% in Women Leadership and Entrepreneurship component are reserved for women candidates.

n: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
q: Are there any seats earmarked for PwD candidates?
a: 3% of the scheme benefits are earmarked for PwD candidates.

n: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
q: Is there any income criteria?
a: Up to 25% of seats may be earmarked under traditional skilling and up to 15% under other components for non minority EWS category.

n: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
q: How to apply for scheme/courses?
a: Access your dashboard on SIDH portal to find PM VIKAS scheme and job roles. Use filters such as scheme, mode, and sector to find suitable courses or batches.

n: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
q: How to apply for a training batch?
a: Choose a batch for your preferred job role and submit your interest or application. You may select up to five batches, which will be reviewed by the training partner /training centre.

n: Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan
q: How to finalize enrolment?
a: After approval from the training partner / training centre, accept the invitation through your portal to confirm enrolment. Track your application status under the 'Applications' section.

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: Who launched PM-YASASVI?
a: PM-YASASVI was launched by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India.

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: What is the objective of the scheme?
a: The objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to the OBC, EBC and DNT students studying at post-matriculation or post-secondary stage to enable them to complete their education.

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: What is the scope of scheme?
a: These scholarships shall be available for studies in India only and will be awarded by the Government of State/Union Territory to which the applicant actually belongs, i.e. permanently settled.

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: Who can apply for the scholarships?
a: Indian nationals belonging to Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Economically Backward Classes (EBCs), and Denotified Nomadic Tribes (DNTs) as notified by the Central Govt./State Govt./UT Admin are eligible.

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: What does 'Group 1' mean?
a: "Group 1: Degree and Post Graduate level professional courses" shall mean all Professional courses in Medicine, Engineering, Technology, Planning, Architecture, Design, Fashion Technology, Agriculture, Veterinary & Allied Sciences, Management, Business Finance /Administration, Computer Science/ Applications (ii) Post Graduate Diploma courses in various branches of Management & Medicine(iii) C.A./I.C.W.A./C.S./1.C.F.A. etc. (iv) M.Phil., Ph.D. and Post-Doctoral Programmes (D.Lit., D.Sc. etc.) of Group I, Group II and Group Ill courses. (v) L.L.B, Integrated LL B, L.L.M (vi) Commercial Pilot Lic

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: What does 'Group 2' mean?
a: "Group 2: Other Professional Courses leading to Degree, Diploma, Certificate" shall mean all Professional Courses leading to Degree, M Ed. / M. Pharma., Diploma, Certificate in areas like Pharmacy (B Pharma.), Nursing(B Nursing), BFS, other para-medical branches like rehabilitation, diagnostics etc., Mass Communication, Hotel Management & Catering, Travel/Tourism/Hospitality Management, Interior Decoration, Nutrition& Dietetics, Commercial Art, Financial Services (e.g. Banking, Insurance, Taxation etc.) for which entrance qualification is minimum Sr. Secondary (10+2) and Vocational stream, ITI

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: What does 'Group 3' mean?
a: "Group 3: Graduate and Post Graduate course" shall mean: courses not covered under Group 1& Group 2 e.g. BA / B.Sc. / B.Com etc. M.A/ M. Sc./ M.Com etc.

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: What does 'Group 4' mean?
a: "Group 4: All post-matriculation (Post Class X level) non-degree courses" shall mean All post-matriculation level non-degree courses for which entrance qualification is High School (Class X), e.g. Senior secondary certificate (class XI and XII ); both general and vocational stream, ITI courses, 3-year diploma courses in Polytechnics, etc.

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: What does 'Freeship Card' mean?
a: "Freeship Card" shall mean a card issued by the State Govt./UT Administration that entitles a student eligible for a scholarship under this Scheme, to take admission in an institution, without pre-payment of tuition fee and hostel fee.

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: How will the scholarship amount be disbursed?
a: The entire scholarship amount, including tuition fees, academic allowance, and any other admissible allowance, will be paid directly into the students' bank accounts ONLY through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), preferably through an Aadhaar Based Payment System (Aadhaar Payment Bridge).

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: How are students pursuing professional courses like CA/ICWA/CS/ICFA treated for academic allowance?
a: Students pursuing CA/ICWA/CS/ICFA shall be treated as day scholars for the purpose of academic allowance.

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: Are students studying through correspondence/online courses eligible for academic allowance?
a: No, students studying through correspondence/online courses shall not be eligible for academic allowance.

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: Will tuition fees be paid to online/correspondence students?
a: Yes, tuition fees shall be paid to online/correspondence students.

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: What courses are covered under the scholarship?
a: The scholarships are available for all recognized post-matriculation or post-secondary courses pursued in recognized institutions.

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: What educational qualifications are required for eligibility?
a: Eligible candidates must have passed the Matriculation or higher secondary or any higher examination from a recognized University or Board of Secondary Education.

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: Are post-graduate medical students eligible for the scholarship?
a: Yes, but only if they are not allowed to practice during the period of their course.

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: Is there a limit on the number of scholarships per family?
a: Yes, only two boys of the same parents/guardian will be entitled to receive scholarships. However, this restriction does not apply to girls.

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: Can scholarship holders hold other scholarships simultaneously?
a: No, scholarship holders cannot hold any other scholarship/stipend. They can, however, accept free lodging, grants, or ad-hoc monetary help for specific purposes.

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: What is the income eligibility criterion for employed and unemployed students?
a: Employed students whose income combined with their parents/guardians does not exceed [?]2.50 lakh per annum, and unemployed students whose parents/guardians' income does not exceed [?]2.50 lakh per annum are eligible.

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: How long is the scholarship payable?

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: Can the scholarship be renewed if a scholar is unable to appear in the annual examination due to illness?

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: Is there a provision for renewal if a scholar fails in Group I course examination?

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: Is Aadhaar authentication compulsory for renewals?
a: Yes, Aadhaar authentication is compulsory at the time of renewals if not provided earlier at the time of admission.

n: PM-YASASVI: Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: What is the scope and coverage of the scheme?
a: The Scheme will operate in all the institutions notified by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment for every financial year 2021-22 onwards. | The scholarship, once awarded, will continue till the completion of the course, subject to satisfactory performance of the student. The students are required to apply for scholarships every year even in case of renewal also.

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students

a: The scheme is fully funded by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, on a 100% basis.

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: What is covered under the scholarship for OBC/EBC/DNT students in notified institutions?
a: The scholarship covers various expenses including full tuition fee and non-refundable charges, living expenses, books and stationery, and provision for a computer/laptop.

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: How much financial assistance is provided for tuition fees?
a: For private sector institutions, the ceiling is [?]2.00 lakh per annum per student. For private sector flying clubs for Commercial Pilot Training and Type Rating Courses, it's [?]3.72 lakhs per annum per student.

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: What living expenses are covered under the scholarship?
a: Beneficiaries receive [?]3,000 per month per student to cover living expenses.

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: Are there provisions for books and stationery?

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: Is there assistance provided for acquiring a computer/laptop?
a: Yes, students are entitled to a latest computer/laptop of a reputed brand with accessories like UPS and printer, limited to [?]45,000 per student as one-time assistance during the course.

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students

a: The scholarship becomes payable immediately after a student secures admission and starts attending classes.

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: How are living expenses, books, stationery, and computer/laptop with accessories provided?
a: These expenses are directly transferred to the student by the Central Government through Direct Benefit Transfer mode.

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students

a: Students with a total annual family income from all sources up to [?]2.50 lakhs are eligible.

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class College Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: Who is eligible for this scheme?

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: How are Top Class Schools identified under the scheme?
a: Top Class Schools (TCSs) are selected by a committee chaired by the Joint Secretary (BC), with representation from the Department of School Education and NITI Aayog. These schools must consistently achieve 100% pass rates in Classes 10th and 12th.

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: What expenses does the scholarship cover?
a: The scholarship provides grants for tuition fees, hostel fees, and other charges required by the school, up to a maximum of [?]75,000/- per annum per student for Classes 9 and 10, and [?]1,25,000/- per annum per student for Classes 11 and 12.

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: Are there any conditions of eligibility for students?
a: Yes, besides belonging to eligible categories and studying in designated Top Class Schools, students must have a household income below [?]2.5 lakhs. Additionally, they must maintain a bank account and provide all necessary details while applying for the scheme.

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
q: Is there any reservation for girls under the scheme?
a: Yes, at least 30% of the scholarships are reserved for girls, ensuring gender inclusivity in the distribution of benefits.

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students

a: Funds are directly transferred into the beneficiaries' bank accounts through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode. Payments are made in installments and are released before the 15th of August each year.

n: PM-YASASVI: Top Class School Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students

n: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
q: What is the objective of the Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana (PMAGY)?
a: The main objective of PMAGY is the integrated development of Scheduled Caste (SC) majority villages through the convergent implementation of existing schemes and additional support using gap-filling funds for unmet needs.

n: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
q: When was the PMAGY launched and in which states was it initially implemented?
a: PMAGY was launched in 2009-10 on a pilot basis in 1,000 villages across five states: Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh, and Assam.

n: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
q: What is the eligibility criteria for a village to be selected under PMAGY?
a: Villages must: | - Have more than 50% SC population.- Have a total population greater than 500. Selection is done in descending order based on the percentage of SC population.

n: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
q: What is the vision of an ‘Adarsh Gram’?
a: An Adarsh Gram is a model village where all residents have access to basic services like housing, sanitation, health, education, employment, and no caste-based discrimination, enabling them to live a life of dignity.

n: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
q: What kind of financial support is provided under PMAGY?
a: Each selected village receives ₹20 lakh as Central Assistance under PMAGY for gap-filling activities not covered by existing schemes. The balance amount of ₹1 lakh per village would be for administrative and other expenses

n: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
q: What are the key focus areas of development under PMAGY?
a: Development under PMAGY focuses on: | - Physical infrastructure (roads, electricity, water) | - Sanitation & environment | - Social infrastructure and human development | - Livelihood and skill development | - Social harmony and dignity

n: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
q: Are only Central Government schemes used for development under PMAGY?
a: No. PMAGY emphasizes convergent implementation of both Central and State/UT Government schemes, along with gap-filling funds to cover uncovered areas.

n: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
q: What is meant by ‘gap-filling’ under PMAGY?
a: ‘Gap-filling’ refers to activities and needs of the village that are not covered under existing schemes. PMAGY provides funds specifically to fulfill these unmet needs.

n: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
q: What are the benefits to residents of a PMAGY village?
a: Residents benefit from: | - All-weather roads, safe drinking water, electricity | - Sanitary living conditions and solid waste management | - Functional schools, Anganwadi centers, health centers | - Skill training, employment opportunities, and social equality

n: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
q: How does PMAGY promote social harmony and inclusion?
a: The scheme works to eliminate untouchability, caste-based discrimination, and promotes dignity, equal rights, and active community participation through institutions like Gram Sabha, Mahila Mandals, and Youth Clubs.

n: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
q: What is the minimum Scheduled Caste population percentage required for a village to be considered eligible under this developmental scheme?
a: Villages must have more than 40% Scheduled Caste population as per the latest available Census data to qualify for selection. Additionally, the total population should be ≥ 500 persons for eligibility consideration.

n: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
q: How much financial assistance is provided to newly selected villages for infrastructure development and what additional support is available for administrative activities?
a: Newly selected villages receive ₹20,00,000/- for Gap-filling infrastructure development activities that cannot be covered through convergence with other schemes. An additional ₹1,00,000/- per village is allocated for administrative expenses including technical resource support, capacity building, awareness generation, and Management Information System maintenance.

n: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
q: What happens to villages that have already completed the initial development phase and wish to continue further improvement after five years?
a: Villages that successfully implement their Village Development Plan and complete the five-year monitoring period can receive an additional round of funding. This includes ₹9,50,000/- for Gap-filling component and ₹50,000/- for administrative expenses to support continuous development initiatives.

n: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
q: Which online portal must be used for need assessment data entry and Village Development Plan preparation throughout the implementation process?
a: All activities including need assessment, data collection, gap analysis, and Village Development Plan preparation must be conducted through the centralized web portal https://pmagy.gov.in. This portal provides all necessary formats and auto-generates the comprehensive Village Development Plan.

n: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
q: What is the time limit for utilizing the Gap-filling funds received by selected villages and what happens during the extended monitoring period?
a: Gap-filling funds must be utilized within 2 years from the date of release for all infrastructure development activities. However, convergent implementation continues for an additional 3 years to ensure maintenance of basic developmental milestones and stabilization of socio-economic indicators.

n: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
q: Who heads the Village Level Convergence Committee and what are the mandatory membership requirements for effective scheme implementation?
a: The Village Level Convergence Committee is headed by the Sarpanch or Pradhan of the village and must include all Scheduled Caste members of the Gram Panchayat, Anganwadi Workers, ASHA workers, and other concerned line officials. One Scheduled Caste member serves as Member Secretary.

n: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
q: How many socio-economic developmental indicators must be monitored and across how many different domains are these indicators distributed?
a: Villages must monitor 50 socio-economic developmental monitorable indicators distributed across 10 domains including drinking water and sanitation, education, health and nutrition, social security, rural roads and housing, electricity and clean fuel, agricultural practices, financial inclusion, digitization, and livelihood and skill development.

n: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
q: What minimum score must a village achieve on the monitorable indicators to qualify for declaration as an Adarsh Gram?
a: Villages must achieve a score of 70 or above on the monitorable indicators and be declared as Open Defecation Free to qualify for Adarsh Gram declaration. Each indicator can achieve a maximum score of 2, making the total possible score 100.

n: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
q: What is the expected convergence ratio that State Governments must ensure with other schemes to maximize development impact?
a: State Governments and Union Territory Administrations are expected to ensure convergence of at least 3 to 4 times of Gap-filling funds from existing Central and State Schemes or matching grants to achieve comprehensive village saturation with basic infrastructure.

n: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
q: How frequently must the Gram Sabha conduct social audit of the scheme implementation and what is the purpose of this requirement?
a: The Gram Sabha must undertake social audit of the scheme at least once a year to ensure greater transparency and better utilization of resources, following the same methodology required under Section 17 of the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005.

n: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
q: What are the different formats required for capturing village level data and how do these formats contribute to the overall Village Development Plan?
a: The need assessment requires Format I for village level data, Format II for village level infrastructural needs, Format III-A for family and individual needs, and Format III-B for consolidation. The final Village Development Plan consists of Formats I, IV, V and VI.

n: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
q: Which committee at the district level is responsible for appraising and approving the Village Development Plans prepared by villages?
a: The District Level Project Appraisal cum Convergence Committee headed by the District Collector is responsible for appraising Village Development Plans. This committee ensures robust planning with adequate convergence and potential for desired improvements in monitorable indicators.

n: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
q: What specific activities are funded exclusively through Gap-filling component and what types of activities require convergence with other schemes?
a: Gap-filling funds cover only non-recurring infrastructure developmental requirements for community purposes that cannot be met under existing Central or State Government schemes. All other developmental activities must be implemented through convergence with relevant existing schemes.

n: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram
q: How are the administrative expenses of ₹1,00,000/- per village distributed among different levels of implementation and what is the allocation ratio?
a: The administrative expenses are distributed among Centre, State, District and Village in a ratio of 1:1:1:2. This covers technical resource support, training and capacity building, awareness generation, publicity, and Management Information System development and maintenance at all levels.

n: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin
q: What assistance in convergence with MGNREGA is provided under PMAY-G?
a: In convergence with MGNREGA, the beneficiaries get employment for 95 days. The beneficiaries are paid [?] 90.95 per day for unskilled labor.

n: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin
q: What assistance in convergence with SBM-G is provided under PMAY-G?
a: In convergence with SBM-G, the beneficiaries get assistance for the construction of toilets of up to [?] 12,000.

n: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin
q: How are the beneficiaries for PMAY-G identified?
a: The beneficiaries are identified using parameters from the Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) and verified by the Gram Sabhas.

n: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin
q: How the amount of loan or financial assistance provided to the beneficiary?
a: The amount is transferred directly to the Aadhaar-Linked Bank Account / Post-Office Account of the beneficiary.

n: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin
q: What is the amount and the purpose of loan provided under PMAY-G?
a: A loan up to [?] 70,000/- is provided at 3% lower interest rates) to the beneficiary to build a permanent dwelling.

n: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin
q: Who is the Implementing Agency of PMAY-G?
a: PMAY-G s being implemented by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA).

n: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
q: Is the entire mission implemented as Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS)?
a: Except for the component of Credit Linked Subsidy which is implemented as a Central Sector Scheme, the rest of the mission is implemented as Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS).

n: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
q: I need to know the technical specifications, construction standards of the houses/slums that will be built under this scheme?
a: The houses must conform to the standards provided in National Building Code (NBC) and Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). For a detailed description of the houses/slums, please refer Section-2 of the scheme guidelines: https://pmay-urban.gov.in/uploads/guidelines/60180813309f2-Updated%20guidelines%20of%20PMAY-U.pdf

n: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
q: Are there any sections that would be given preference while providing the benefits?
a: Preference will be given to differently-abled persons, senior citizens, SCs, STs, OBCs, Minority, single women, transgender and other weaker & vulnerable sections of the society.

n: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
q: Will I still be eligible to apply for government’s ongoing or upcoming schemes if I apply for PMAY-U?
a: The benefits of all existing and future rural schemes will not be denied to a beneficiary solely on the grounds that she/he has availed a house under PMAY(U).

n: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
q: I am a beneficiary of PMAY (G) but I am in the permanent waitlist. What are my options?
a: The beneficiaries in the permanent wait list of PMAY (G) will have the flexibility for opting for a house under PMAY(G) or PMAY(U).

n: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
q: How do I know if my town is covered under the scheme?
a: You can visit https://pmay-urban.gov.in/pmayprogress to check the same. Alternatively, you can visit https://pmay-urban.gov.in/ and head to "City Wise Progress".

n: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
q: For how am I required to be residing in an urban area to become a beneficiary under this scheme?
a: The States/UTs, at their discretion, may decide a cut-off date on which beneficiaries need to be a resident of that urban area for being eligible to take benefits under the scheme.

n: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
q: Will central assistance be provided for rehabilitation of dwellers from slums built on private land?
a: No, slums built on private land are not covered under central assistance.

n: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
q: Is there a private entity authorised by MoHUA to collect fee from the beneficiary under PMAY-U?
a: No private entity/persons have been authorised by MoHUA to collect this fee from any beneficiary under this scheme.

n: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
q: How do I know if a field in the application form is mandatory?
a: The mandatory fields have a red asterisk (*) mark at the end.

n: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
q: How do I check my application status?
a: There are two ways in which the applicant can check his/her application status: | Method-1: Using Assessment ID. | Step 1: Log on to the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana website: http://pmaymis.gov.in/Track_Application_Status.aspx or go to the 'Citizen Application' option and then choose the 'Check Status' button. | Step 2: When you hit the track button, there will be two options displayed: 'By Name, Father's Name & Mobile No' and 'By Assessment ID'. | Step 3: Choose the 'By Assessment ID' option. | Step 4: Enter the Assessment ID & Mobile Number that was assigned when the form was filled and submit

n: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
q: What Is Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP)?
a: 'Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP)' is a campaign launched by the Department of Pharmaceuticals in association with Central Pharma Public Sector Undertakings to provide quality medicines at affordable prices to the masses through dedicated outlets called 'Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendra'. These provide generic medicines at a much lower price. The potency of these medicines is the same as compared to expensive branded medicines available on the open market.

n: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
q: What Is A Generic Medicine?
a: Generic drugs are marketed under a non-proprietary or approved name rather than a proprietary or brand name. Generic drugs are equally effective and inexpensive compared to their branded counterparts.

n: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
q: What Is PMBI?
a: PMBI (Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of India) has been established under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Govt. of India, with the support of all the CPSUs for co-coordinating procurement, supply, and marketing of generic drugs through the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras.

n: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
q: How The Quality, Safety And Efficacy Of Medicines Are Ensured?
a: The quality, safety, and efficacy of medicines are ensured by getting each batch of medicines procured from CPSUs as well as private suppliers tested from NABL-approved laboratories and conforming to the required standards before the same are supplied to Super stockists /Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras from the warehouse of PMBI.

n: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
q: Are Generic Drugs As Effective As Branded Ones?
a: Generic drugs have the same efficacy and therapeutic value as that of branded medicines.

n: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
q: How Do Generic Medicines Benefit The Patients?
a: By taking generic medicines, a patient can reduce his/her expenditure on medicines drastically.

n: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
q: What Are The Medicines Available From Pradhan Mantri Janaushadhi Kendras And What Are Their Prices?
a: The endeavor of PMBI is to make available all therapeutic medicines at Jan Aushadhi Stores. A list of medicines with their MRP which are presently available is given under the heading "PMBJP Products- Therapeutic groups" on the website of PMBI. More medicines are being added to this list.

n: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
q: How Many Pradhan Mantri Janaushadhi Kendras Have Been Opened And What Are Their Locations?
a: More than 8604 are currently functional. A list of State-wise / District-wise PMBJK along with their locations are available under the heading "PMBJP => PMBJP Kendra" on the website of PMBI.

n: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
q: What Is The Timing (Opening And Closing) Of The Pradhan Mantri Janaushadhi Kendras?
a: The normal working hours of PMBJK are 8 AM to 8 PM.

n: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
q: How The Medicines Are Procured And Supplied To Pradhan Mantri Janaushadhi Kendras?
a: Medicines are procured through an open tender system from private manufacturers as well as CPSUs. Each batch of procured medicines are duly tested from impanelled NABL laboratories and sent to Kendra through distribution network.

n: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
q: Who Can Open A Pradhan Mantri Janaushadhi Kendras?
a: Individual entrepreneur / Proprietor | Partnership | Charitable Institute/Hospital | NGO/ Trust/ Society | Government/ Government Nominated Agency | Any Other (Please specify)

a: PM ECRG is a one-time grant and carries a maximum research grant of Rs. 60 Lakhs (excluding overheads) for a period of three years. The research grant covers equipment, research personnel, consumables, travel and contingency apart from overheads.

n: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant

n: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant

n: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant

n: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant

International travel is permitted within this limit.

n: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
q: Are there any limits on contingency expenditure for the project?
a: Yes, the expenditure under the contingency head is also limited to Rs. 3 Lakh for a three-year project, or proportionately lower for shorter projects.

n: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant

n: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant

n: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant

n: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant

n: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant

n: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant

n: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme

n: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme

a: Answer: PMEGP stands for Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme, which is a credit-linked subsidy scheme launched by the Ministry of MSME, Government of India, to generate employment opportunities in the country. The main objective of the scheme is to create self-employment opportunities for unemployed youth and women entrepreneurs in rural and urban areas.

n: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
q: Who Is Eligible To Apply For PMEGP Scheme, And What Is The Age Limit For The Applicants?

n: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme

The application procedure involves filling up the application form, attaching the necessary documents, and submitting it along with the project report.

n: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme

a: Answer: The PMEGP scheme supports various types of projects, including manufacturing, service, and business projects. The projects should be viable and have the potential to generate employment opportunities.

n: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
q: How Much Financial Assistance Can I Expect To Receive Under The PMEGP Scheme, And What Is The Repayment Period?
a: Answer: Under the PMEGP scheme, financial assistance is provided in the form of a subsidy, which ranges from 15% to 35% of the project cost, depending on the category of the applicant. The remaining amount can be obtained as a bank loan. The repayment period for the loan is generally 3 to 7 years.

n: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme

a: Answer: No, an individual can apply for only one project under the PMEGP scheme. However, a group of individuals can apply for a group project, subject to a maximum of 10 members.

n: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme

a: Answer: The documents required for PMEGP scheme application include a project report, proof of identity and address, caste certificate (if applicable), educational qualification certificate, and bank account details.

n: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme

a: Answer: The processing time for the PMEGP scheme application varies from state to state and depends on various factors such as the completeness of the application, the availability of funds, and the number of applications received.

n: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme

a: Answer: No, the PMEGP scheme is meant for setting up a new business or for expanding an existing business. An existing business is not eligible for financial assistance under the PMEGP scheme.

n: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme

n: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)

a: Coverage is available for up to 14 days post-harvest for crops kept in "cut & spread" condition in the field, specifically for damage from cyclonic/unseasonal rains. You must report the damage immediately.

n: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
q: What is the exact premium rate for Kharif paddy, and how is the government subsidy calculated?
a: Farmers pay 2% of the sum insured for Kharif food crops. The difference between the actuarial premium rate and farmer's share is jointly subsidized by Central and State governments equally.

n: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
q: If a drought prevents me from sowing crops despite preparation, what percentage of compensation can I claim?
a: You can claim up to 25% of the sum insured under prevented sowing coverage, provided the majority of farmers in your notified area were also prevented from sowing due to adverse conditions.

n: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
q: I farm in Himachal Pradesh. Do I need to pay any premium for my apple crop under PMFBY?
a: No, farmers in Himachal Pradesh, along with other North-Eastern states and Jammu & Kashmir, receive 100% premium subsidy from the government for all notified crops.

n: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
q: Can I claim compensation if my entire village faced crop damage from a landslide, but neighboring villages were unaffected?
a: Yes, PMFBY covers localized calamities like landslides on an individual farm basis, even if the damage is isolated to specific areas within the notified region.

n: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)

a: PMFBY aims to process and settle claims within two months of harvest, provided all documentation is complete and damage assessment is finalized.

n: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)

a: For loanee farmers, coverage is compulsory but not automatic. You must ensure your bank has processed your PMFBY enrollment within the specified timeframe.

n: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)

a: You can visit a nearby CSC or bank branch to submit your premium payment. Keep proof of your online payment attempt for any deadline-related disputes.

n: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)

n: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)

a: Natural fire is covered, but damage from wild animals isn't. For fire spreading from neighboring fields, you must provide evidence that it wasn't due to negligence.
